CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the special meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:31 p.m.
on Tuesday, November 30, 2021 with all Commissioners and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Fitzsimmons.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Jacqueline Borja, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto,
  Jorge Herrera, Riaz (Rick) Khan and Chasity Jennings-Nuñez
Commissioners Absent:  None.

ANNOUNCMENTS

Recreation Supervisor Matthew Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

HEAR COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 30, 2021
   3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A motion was made by Commissioner Fitzsimmons and seconded by
  Commissioner Brenhaug to approve the minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular
  Meeting for October 26, 2021.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. UPDATE ON THE NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH CELEBRATION

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez read the proclamation for Native American Heritage month
  that was presented by the Mayor and City Council at the November 2, 2021 council
  meeting.

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, provided an update on the
  celebrations and programs offered throughout the City in support of Native
  American Heritage Month. This included programs offered at the San Gabriel
  Public Library, essay contest offered by the City, and the Native American Heritage
  Month Celebration video developed by City staff.

  The Commission discussed possible barriers to participation and ways to increase
  participation for the essay contest in future years.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez thanked Chief Morales and Chief Salas for participating in
  the Native American Heritage Month Celebration Video. She also provided thanks
  to City staff Christin and Victoria for their work on recording and editing the video.
  Finally, she provided thanks to the staff at the San Gabriel Public Library for their
  efforts in offering programs in honor of Native American Heritage Month.

  Public Comment: None

  B. LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT STATEMENT

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, provided an update based on
  the last Land Acknowledgement Statement (LAS) Advisory Committee meeting
  held November 10, 2021. Matthew shared that Chief Morales and Chief Salas joined
  the LAS meeting. They were provided an opportunity to respond to predetermined

HEAR COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 30, 2021
   questions prepared by the Committee members. Staff will provide a transcription
  of the responses at the next LAS meeting.

  Commissioner Brenhaug shared that she is excited to have a partnership with the
  indigenous peoples of the area and discover ways in which the City can support
  them, even beyond the LAS.

  Public Comment: None

  C. REVIEW OF THE 2021 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor, reviewed the 2021 Annual
  Workplan Progress Update memo, included in the agenda packet.

  The commissioners reviewed the youth engagement survey. A motion to approve
  the youth engagement survey was made by Commissioner Borja and seconded by
  Commissioner Brenhaug.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  The commissioners discussed ways in which the survey would be distributed. The
  primary focus would be for youth with distribution beginning in January 2022.
  Once the commission is prepared to release the survey to the boarder public staff
  will determine how the survey can be translated.

  A motion to approve the youth ambassador application with amendments was
  made by Commissioner Goto and seconded by Commissioner Borja.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Borja, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Khan, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None

  The commissioners review the Workplan items to determine items that need to be
  carried over to the 2022 Workplan. It was determined that all items in the Workplan
  with the exception of the items listed under item 5 will be carried over to the 2022
  Workplan. Additionally, all overarching categories will be utilized in the 2022
  Workplan.

  Public Comment: None

HEAR COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  NOVEMBER 30, 2021
   D. DEVELOPMENT OF THE 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  The overall categories will carry into the 2022 workplan. The commissioners
  provided items that they would like to see added into the Workplan.

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Goto shared that she attended a bystander intervention training
  sponsored by the Asian Americans Advancing Justice and the Hollaback!
  organizations and provided information on what was provided during the training.
  She recommended and provided information on a one-hour documentary on PBS
  called Duty Free that focuses on the effects of ageism.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez provided additional information on the Hollaback!
  Organization.

  Vice-Chair Herrera announced the City’s Annual Holiday Tree Lighting event and
  recommended that the commission get together at the end of the year to celebrate
  the Commission’s accomplishments. Chair Jennings-Nuñez recommended that the
  commissioners meet at the tree lighting event. Finally, Vice-Chair Herrera
  encouraged residents to provide public comments.

  Commissioner Khan provided information on the Holiday Basket program which
  serves families in need.

  Public Comment: None

  Staff stated that the January commission meeting is tentatively scheduled to take

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:28 p.m.

DATE:  January 25, 2022

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2022 Draft Annual Workplan

OVERVIEW
The Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission, consisting of 7 members,
was developed by the San Gabriel City Council to address issues of equity, diversity, social
justice, safety, mutual appreciation and respect on an ongoing basis.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community
(the “Purpose”).

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

PURPOSE OF THE ANNUAL WORKPLAN
The annual Workplan presented is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission
and outline the areas of focus for the remainder of 2022. It includes proposed programs
and projects that will be implemented and completed in 2022, some of which may extend
beyond 2022.

DRAFT 2022 WORKPLAN
The draft 2022 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission has
identified as key areas of interest in furtherance of its purpose. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities that the HEAR Commission proposes to include in its Workplan
are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items that the Commission can
explore. It should be noted that staff has indicated in parenthesis the way in which each
action item meets the Commission’s purpose.

  1. Equity Training and Inequities in City Policies (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the
  Commission for Equity)

  2. Community Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Diversity, Mutual Appreciation and Increased Cultural Competency)
  a. Develop and implement programs and events, possibly in partnership with
  the Community Services Commission and Department, that engage and
  educate the community to promote the goals of the HEAR Commission
  i. Examples include: a culturally-diverse movie night, an event to
  celebrate Native American Heritage Month, and a mental health
  forum
  b. Guest speaker(s)/ educational program(s) - during the regular Commission
  meetings (one per month)- which relates to the scope of the Commission
  i. Examples include: Bystander Training, anti-bias training, cultural
  diversity, mental health awareness, low income housing,
  homelessness and other relevant topics
  c. Focus on environmental justice
  d. Promoting the racial equity challenge

  3. Youth Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Diversity
  and Access)
  a. Collect data about the needs of youth in the community utilizing existing
  City platforms
  b. Add two youth liaisons to the current HEAR Commission to enable the youth
  voice to be heard within the community. Each representative would be
  chosen through an application process and selected by the Commission

  4. Community Information (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Access)
